headline: The major coastal storm's worst wind and rain are winding down early Friday, leaving a mild, cloudy Friday with a few showers and lingering minor to locally moderate coastal flooding at the morning high tide.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: In the early hours of Friday the storm's rain and wind ease as a warm front lifts north through New York City; the High Wind Warning and Wind Advisories end at 1 AM. Temperatures climb into the 50s overnight, and fog may form for a while as winds briefly calm, mainly outside the city, before south winds pick back up. Friday stays cloudy with a chance of showers as the storm's upper-level low passes to the northwest, with the best chances north and west of the city; highs reach the mid to upper 50s (possibly cooler under the clouds and showers), with south-southwest winds gusting 25 to 30 mph. Showers may linger over Long Island and Connecticut into Friday evening, then winds turn southwest and stay gusty overnight.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Saturday looks dry as the storm moves off through northern New England, with west winds gusting about 25 to 30 mph that ease Saturday night. Sunday looks dry and calmer. The discussion gives no temperature details for the weekend.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: Showers are likely after midnight Sunday night as a front arrives, with a chance of showers lingering Monday morning. Monday's southwest winds gust about 25 to 30 mph, turning west in the afternoon and northwest Monday night. Tuesday looks dry.

coast: Coastal Flood Warnings run until 6 AM Friday for New York City, Long Island, coastal New Jersey and coastal Connecticut except the southeastern part of the state, after last night's 3 to 4 foot storm surge brought moderate to major flooding, including surge up the Hackensack, Hudson and Passaic rivers. For Friday morning's high tide winds turn southwest, so widespread minor flooding is likely, locally moderate in the back bays of Long Island's south shore; Coastal Flood Advisories cover coastal areas from 6 AM Friday until between noon and 4 PM depending on location. Ocean beaches see 8 to 12 foot breaking waves with beach flooding, dune erosion and possible localized overwashes at high tide that can flood roads and buildings behind the dunes, while the western Sound and Long Island's forks see 3 to 6 foot breakers with dune erosion, splashover and possible isolated damage to shoreline and marina structures. On the water the Storm Warning ends at 1 AM Friday, but a southwest gale is likely on the ocean Friday (Gale Warning until 6 AM Saturday) with a Small Craft Advisory on the Sound, harbor and bays until 6 AM Saturday; winds ease Saturday, are likely below advisory levels Sunday, and southwest to west gales are possible on the ocean again Monday.
watch_for: Friday morning's high tide, with minor to locally moderate flooding, especially Long Island's south shore back bays
Patchy fog early Friday as winds calm behind the warm front
Showers late Sunday night into Monday morning, with gusty winds Monday
confidence: Forecasters are confident the storm winds down early Friday, are less sure about early-morning fog and cloud details, and note Friday could run cooler than forecast under clouds and showers.
